result.note: Tested the India–Zambia critical minerals block and India's copper import position; skipped the analysis on the exploration trap.

questions.prompt: In April 2026, India refused to commit further capital to a cobalt and copper exploration block until the host country guarantees long-term mining rights. Which country allocated this block to India?
questions.explain: India paused investment in the Zambian block, which Zambia allocated in 2025, until Lusaka guarantees long-term tenure. Geologists have finished initial fieldwork, but New Delhi will not move to private-sector extraction without secure rights.
questions.source: India has hit pause on Zambian critical mineral investment, refusing to commit further capital until Lusaka guarantees long-term mining rights.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's critical mineral position, as reported in April 2026:
items: The block Zambia allocated to India for cobalt and copper exploration covers about 9,000 square kilometres.
The 2018 closure of Vedanta's Sterlite Copper smelter turned India from a copper exporter into an importer.
India's copper imports fell 4% in the fiscal year ending March 2025.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong: copper imports rose 4% to 1.2 million tonnes in the fiscal year ending March 2025. India is also pursuing government-to-government deals across Africa and Latin America, including an initial agreement with the Democratic Republic of Congo.
questions.source: India's copper imports rose 4% to 1.2 million tonnes in the fiscal year ending March 2025.
